title: Record the review of phase 3: one finding, fixed
message: Record the review of phase 3: one finding, fixed

title: Give an editor copy its own description of the fallen
message:
Give an editor copy its own description of the fallen

copy_object_strings() duplicated every string that free_object_strings()
frees except char_sdesc, a corpse's description of the fallen. An iedit
of a corpse made an edit copy that shared it with the live corpse; the
commit then freed it from the corpse and again from the edit copy, and
the corpse kept the freed pointer until its decay freed it a third time.
A disconnect during the edit freed it from the edit copy alone, under
the live corpse.

A corpse is an object with no prototype, so on master the same path
freed char_sdesc from free_object_strings_proto() after reading
obj_proto[-1]; a0757112c removed the read and kept the double free.

copy_object_strings() now duplicates char_sdesc. Every copy it fills is
freed by free_object_strings() or free_object_strings_proto(), and both
free char_sdesc, so the copy has to own it.

Test_gameplay_object_editor_copy_frees_an_object_with_no_prototype gives
both objects a description of their own and checks that the target gets
the source's text at an address of its own, then frees both. It fails on
the shared pointer before the change, and under the sanitizer and
memory-check jobs the two frees would meet one block. Review finding on
MR !25.

title: Record phase 3 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !25
message:
Record phase 3 of the object save fixes: built, in review as MR !25

Phase 3's record says what was built, what the check of the other
callers of free_object_strings() showed, why a second test was needed
(the memory-check job has no database), and the verification.

Two defects were found on the way. copy_object() read the prototype
table for an object with no prototype; it is fixed in this merge
request. An OLC save of a prototype leaves its live objects sharing the
prototype's lists; it is work item #30 and joins the plan as phase 7.

title: Copy over an object with no prototype without reading the prototype table
message:
Copy over an object with no prototype without reading the prototype table

copy_object() sent every target through free_object_strings_proto(),
which compares the target's strings with its prototype's. For a target
with no prototype that read obj_proto[-1]: memory before the table, or
an unmapped address. The iedit commit reaches it with any live object
that has no prototype.

copy_object() now does what free_obj() does: an object with no
prototype goes through free_object_strings(), since it owns every string
it has.

Test_gameplay_object_editor_copy_frees_an_object_with_no_prototype
copies over such an object with no prototype table at all. It ends in
SIGSEGV before the change. Found while checking the callers of
free_object_strings() for work item #15.

title: Free the arcane mark of an object with no prototype
message:
Free the arcane mark of an object with no prototype

free_obj() sends an object with no prototype through
free_object_strings(), which freed every string the object owns except
arcane_mark. free_object_strings_proto(), the path of an object with a
prototype, has always freed it. So an unnumbered object lost its mark's
memory when it was extracted: the file and player-row loaders give such
an object a mark from its AMrk line, and the arcane mark spell gives one
to any object.

free_object_strings() now frees the mark. Its other callers free the
object or write over it afterwards, and each of those objects owns its
mark or has none: add_object() copies the edited object over the
prototype, and the OLC cleanup and the iedit commit free the edit copy.
The iedit commit leaked the edit copy's mark the same way.

Test_object_without_a_prototype_frees_its_arcane_mark saves and loads a
marked object through the file loader and extracts both; it needs no
database, so the memory-check job runs it.
Test_object_saves_bind_player_house_and_serialized_text no longer frees
its two marks by hand before extract_obj(). Under valgrind each test
loses two blocks without the fix and none with it.

Work item #15.
